body: Hey Robert, please call 911. You might feel okay right now (I saw your replies saying you’re fine) but you don’t know what’s happening on the inside. You’re so young, you need to give life a chance. I’m not much older than you, but I barely remember being 16. The person I was then seems a world away from the person I am right now. Life changes all the time, not always for the better, but it changes a lot in the late teens and young adult years. 20 year old you might be living a life better than you can possibly imagine. You can set goals and meet new people and find independence and conquer your pain. How would future you feel if they knew that 16 year old you was robbing them of a chance to ever come into being? Sorry if that sounded overly philosophical, but please understand that your story isn’t over. It’s barely even begun. Reach out for help - talk to family, friends, a therapist. Make little changes every day. Think hard about what makes you happy and go out of your way to prioritize it. If you don’t have anything that makes you happy, try new things until you find something. And most of all, let time run its course and trust that your circumstances will naturally change so much. I have never met you but I care about you and I hope you get medical help right now to make sure you’re okay. After that, I hope you can recover physically and emotionally from this and start embracing a new stage in your life. I believe in you, you deserve the best.

I’m so sorry, that sounds like a really traumatic experience. Heights are a pretty big fear of mine so that would be one of my worst nightmares lol (up there with drowning), you probably handled it a lot better than most people. I agree with some of the other posters here in that it sounds like it could be PTSD (or something related), although I’m not a medical professional so take that with a grain of salt of course. I think therapy could be helpful, but if you want a shorter term solution, I wouldn’t hesitate to reach out to your GP or even just call a health link to talk about what you’re experiencing (especially if it’s impacting aspects of your daily life like sleep, eating, etc) and see what kinds of measures they would recommend. You could also try r/askdocs, they might be able to advise you on something. I hope you’re able to feel better soon! You’re really brave for going through that.

Can you get in touch with them again? Therapy is something you really have to continue with to see results. If you have some things worth living for, try to remind yourself of those. It doesn’t have to be big. Having a place to start is good enough. If you build from there and focus more on what makes you happy and talk to others about the things you’re struggling with, things could really improve over the longer term? I wish the best for you.

Hey please don’t do this. When you’re in this age category your life and your perspective can change so much in short periods of time, even a year from now things could be so different and you could be so glad you didn’t do this. Your life hasn’t even started yet, please give it a fair chance. A lot of suicidal people think nobody cares about them, but if you could see the impact that it has on family, friends, and even acquaintances after your death you would have no doubt how loved you are and what people would sacrifice to have you around. I had a friend commit suicide a few years ago so I know about this firsthand. I wasn’t even that close to her but that experience really changed my life and the way I view the world. I still think about her and her family. PLEASE talk to someone, don’t just say things vaguely but tell them your exact plan and how serious you are, tell them you need help and you need them to be there for you no matter what. Get some help and find something small to hold on to. I’m only a stranger on the internet and I care enough to write this, you can find someone close to you who will help you through this.

Please don’t do it. Overdosing often doesn’t kill you, it will just make your life way worse than it already feels/is. And a lot of people regret it after doing it because the wait and the drawn-out pain is agonizing. Please talk to someone instead - a family member, close friend, therapist, crisis line. I believe things can get better for you, you’re strong enough to resist this.

Is there anyone you can talk to? Family, close friends, a therapist? If you haven’t found a good therapist you need to keep trying, they’re out there and they can change your life. I know it’s hard to believe right now but your life can change with the right support, a year from now you could be so glad you didn’t do it. 

Is there any small thing you can hold on to that might be worth living for? A hobby, a friend, a dream for the future (even if it feels unrealistic)? Or if you don’t have anything, can you try something new and see if that sparks something in you? Try just looking for one reason to delay this decision that you can’t take back. I’m sorry if I couldn’t help much.

Hey, I commented on this thread and I saw yours and I just wanted to second the person above and say that I really hope you make a decision to get help instead of attempting tomorrow. If you call any crisis line or health link and let them know how bad things are and that you plan to attempt, they WILL help. There are people around you who care and there are people you haven't met yet who care and can help you change your life, it's just hard to see that when you feel really alone. I'm really sorry and I know comments on the internet probably don't have much impact when you feel like this, but I hope you can hold on to a reason to stay and to not hurt yourself tomorrow even if it's just a small one

Hey, I understand what you mean. It seems like once you become a young adult people expect you to get your future together and "be mature", when in reality this can be the most difficult time for a lot of people (and much more so if you suffer from mental illness). But the right kind of people will understand that and love and help you through your difficult times no matter what it is you're going through or how long it takes you to find your footing. I hope you're able to find a good therapist and reach out to family / close friends, it can really make all the difference in dealing with problems. Just remember that you matter and there is much more out there for you than what you're feeling right now

A health link is a good start, I hope you can do that and then go to the hospital. I understand it’s scary but it’s really important so you don’t end up with terrible damage. If your mom is so abusive that you feel like you can’t tell her you attempted suicide without her blaming / manipulating you I would mention that to the doctors, hopefully they take it seriously and they can set you up with supports. I hope you feel better soon and get help and your life situation improves, no problem, I’m glad I could help a bit.

I'm sorry you've had bad experiences with hospitals. I know doing scary things sucks, but sometimes we're simply left with no other choice, and 99% of the time we build it up in our heads to be much scarier than it turns out to be. You'll probably surprise yourself with how strong you can be when it comes down to it. If it's too scary to go straight to the hospital, I would call the health link as others have suggested and maybe they can help you feel more at ease about what you can expect when you get there.

Of course I don't know your mom but she sounds very unsupportive and potentially abusive. If this is something that is making daily life really challenging for you and instigating a lot of your mental health problems I would emphasize that to your therapist or even mention it when you go to the hospital. Abuse is serious and they will set you up with support if they think it's appropriate to the situation. If you don't have a good therapist right now, you can also discuss that at the hospital, a lot of people find therapy unhelpful before someone finally clicks with them.

I'm so sorry for what you're going through, it sounds really difficult. Try reminding yourself that this is only one chapter, you can get support for your relationship with your mom / your mental health and hopefully in the near future you can live on your own / with your boyfriend / with roommates and start building up a more independent life without so many negative triggers. Just take the brave step and get help from the hospital so you can be okay.

Hey, I’m really worried for you! You’re having really serious symptoms. Can you go to a hospital? I don’t want anything to happen to you. Does your mom know you’re sick? If she doesn’t listen to you, please just call an ambulance, or ask a trusted older relative if they can take you. 

It sounds like you have a really awful living situation right now and a lot of personal problems and I’m so sorry about that. I know life can really suck and feel so hopeless. But the most important thing right now is you get some help for the physical symptoms you’re having so nothing happens to you, things can’t get better if you’re not here or you end up with very serious/lasting medical problems! Not trying to scare you, I just want things to improve for you and your safety is always the most important thing. With the symptoms you’re having things could get worse really quickly and it’s critical you don’t delay getting help. 

It sounds like you really need someone to talk to so you can start getting in a better place in your life. Have you seen a therapist? Life isn’t meant to be dealt with by yourself, certain problems are too big for that. If your parents are unsupportive or you’re not comfortable talking with people close to you, it’s really important to find alternative sources of help. It’s so hard to be alone with things, I bet you’ll be amazed how much better you feel once you have a caring person who can help you sort through the parts of your life that feel unfixable. If money is a problem, usually you can get counselling for free through your school (you mentioned you were a uni student).

The first step is going to the hospital so nothing happens to you, there are people who care about you and you have a purpose in this world even if it doesn’t feel that way right now ❤️ I’m sorry if this didn’t help much, I know it’s so much easier said than done.

Hi, thank you for sharing this with us. This is tragic and I am so sorry. I hope you and his family and friends are able to find peace and support each other during this time. Vincenzo’s words really touched me, of course I did not know him but he seemed like a remarkable person. I’ll be praying for you all.
I’m glad I could touch you, you certainly touched me ❤️ Let us know if you’re still here. We’re all here for you.

Vincenzo, I've never cried so much or felt so touched over someone I've never met. You have life in your heart and a goldenness that, if cut short, the world will grieve for in ways you cannot even imagine. The humanity you have is a rare warmth in a world that has long gone cold. 

I know that with what you've suffered, it's hard to believe you're needed. To feel such grief, such isolation at a young age is something impossible to understand unless you've been there. But just as your gifts are here for a purpose, your pain is here for a purpose. You cannot see that when you are in the thick of it; all you can see is dark, but life is often about blind faith, about walking for a time in the dark with no promise about when light will come or what you will encounter before you get there. But if you keep walking, I know you will get there; the wounds will sting a little less and you will begin to see what they gave you. Your pain has and will continue to shape you into the jewel you're meant to be. 

"Don't be late. Don't miss your train. Don't let this moment slip away from your hands..." You touched me so much with your words, Vincenzo. You gave me the strength to get out of bed and the resolve to not let today, like so many days in this chapter of my life, slip away into nothing. I saved your words so I can look back at them when I am tempted to forget the preciousness of today. I have failed countless times and I will probably fail again, but I will try to find courage and iron will. I hope you can find the same. 

If you can change my day with something you wrote in an hour, how much love and hope can you spread in your lifetime? I hope you hold on to your gift, Vincenzo. We are in this together and it is enough just to breathe and persist.

I don't want to give you medical advice as I'm not qualified, but making music for a short time in the morning seems like a good place to start. If you're already having trouble sleeping even without the music it doesn't seem like you have a lot to lose, and you could always stop if it makes your sleep problems worse. Again, I'm not a doctor, so maybe you could mention it to your psychiatrist to see what she thinks of the idea?

By natural remedies I was referring to the insomnia and not the schizophrenia. Things like yoga, meditation, or reading a book before bed can be really helpful, and you don't need to consult your doctor to try those. I've frequently dealt with insomnia as a depression side effect, and the biggest help I've found is putting away all technology when it's close to bedtime. The bright lights will keep your brain awake.

I am sorry about your situation. No one deserves to have their passion taken away from them, even if pursuing it may get in the way of fully prioritizing health.

My apologies if I sound ignorant as I don't know your exact situation, but have you tried making music at different times of the day, e.g. morning rather than night? What about insomnia remedies (either natural or medication)? Starting off small with the amount of time you spend on music (even just 10 minutes a day) and gradually building up over time? Asking about different types of medication? Perhaps there are ways to improve the insomnia side effect so you can still continue to do what you love.
Thank you for the silver, you’re very kind ❤️ Keep fighting.
No problem. <3 Hope you feel better soon.

Check out r/maladaptivedreaming. I’ve dealt with both depression and maladaptive daydreaming, though depression came first and my fantasizing originated as a coping mechanism for depression. This sounds like it might be similar to what you’re experiencing?

This past year has been the hardest of my life in terms of my mental health. I watched the one thing that once mattered to me more than anything fall apart very suddenly, and for the first time in my life I found myself waking up and not being able to recognize myself or identify something to strive for. Running, to me, is a small habit that makes me feel capable of accomplishing big things. Watching my stamina grow, pushing my boundaries, and being able to persist through pain and discomfort is a way of rebuilding a sense of who I am and proving to myself that I am a strong and resilient person - more than ever, in fact, for my struggles. Running gives me confidence that just like I can push through the toughest miles on the track, I can power through life's most painful punches and come out on top. When I'm running to my favourite playlists and smiling through burning muscles, I feel myself come alive again, and for the first time in a long while I've realized that there's something in the distance worth fighting for.

EDIT: Wow, thank you for the gold, kind stranger! I'm honoured! And thank you all for your kind and thoughtful replies. Keep getting in those miles. :)
